_meta.title: Catalogue of the sources cited by the record corpus
_meta.scope: The works and observers that records cite: standard histories, chronicles, veritable records, classical scholarly works and, for the modern period, named astronomers. An entry gives the title in whichever languages the work actually has one, the people responsible for it, a statement of responsibility where that is not a matter of transmission, and the editions consulted. Records cite an entry by key and do not repeat the title; the chapter, leaf or year cited sits with the record. Where the corpus works from a translation or from a quotation in another book, the edition consulted is marked as such, following the Chicago Manual of Style, 18th edition, section 14.260.
_meta.fields: key = source identifier. title = titles by language, with zh-Hans and zh-Hant for works that genuinely have a Chinese title, rom for the romanisation or the Latin-script title and en for the English title, and ja, fr, es and it only where that locale prints a form of its own (an edition named in a note); omitted entirely for an observer entry (optional). form = how a note sets the title when it cites the entry: book (the default; italics or Chinese book-title marks), part (a chapter or book of a work, set like a book), article (quotation marks) or edition (plain type); written only on an entry a note cites (optional). author = the people responsible, each with name in its own script, rom for the romanisation, role (comp, ed, trans, annot, obs, attr), dates of life or activity, and kind set to group for an institution or collective; omitted entirely where the work is genuinely anonymous (optional). attribution = a statement of responsibility that is not a matter of transmission, such as the institution behind an observation, a corroborating witness or a description of an anonymous author (optional). editions = the editions of the work, each with kind (orig, crit, facsim for a direct citation, trans or quot for an indirect one, cite for a bare reference), consulted set to true on exactly one of them, by for the translator, editor or intermediary, title, year, url, license, and locus_url as a template for citing a single chapter (optional). genre = the source's class, a value from build/lib/genre_taxonomy: the standard-history subgenres (history_astronomy, history_annals, history_wuxing, veritable_records, huiyao, chronicle), 'newspaper' (whose per-record leaf — dispatch, report, eyewitness, scientific, feuilleton, editorial, notice — is decided from the text or declared in the record's own genre field, not stored here), the learned classes (observatory_report, learned_society) and the miscellany (poetry, cuneiform, diary, letter, classic). It groups the README's class table and tells the Chinese translation which register to write; the 报刊 line keeps the newspaper register and Han numerals where a chronicle or a journal does not (optional).
_meta.provenance: Compiled and maintained by hand. The first version was aggregated from the bibliographic fields of an earlier form of the corpus. Entries are sorted by key, one per line; build/stage3_records/format_sources.py rewrites the table in that layout and validate_records.py rejects any other.
